$comment: Single source of truth mapping the files in this folder to rows in masterclass_resources.
resources/ holds PUBLISHED files only, and students only ever receive PDFs.
Word documents are the editing format and live in active-word-notes/; they are
never listed here and never uploaded. Adding or updating a resource is:
1. edit (or drop) the .docx in active-word-notes/week-NN/<category>/
2. pwsh -File tools/docx-to-pdf.ps1      exports the PDF into resources/
3. add an entry below, then `npm run resources:sync`
Files that have no Word source (slide decks, images, code) go straight into
resources/week-NN/<category>/ and are listed here as normal.
An entry is either a file or a link. A link has no folder to be filed in, so
it states its own week and category, and `liveLink: true` marks it as the
week's live class - the button students see at the top of the week. Only one
live link per week; syncing again replaces that week's link rather than
adding a second.
Each entry:
file        path relative to resources/ (its folder decides week and category)
url         an https link, instead of `file` - then `week` and `category` are required
liveLink    true if this is the week's live class link (links only)
type        for links: 'link' (default), 'github' or 'video'
title       what students see in the LMS
description one line explaining what it is
objective   what a student should be able to do after using it
required    true if the week cannot be completed without it
order       sort position within its category
published   false keeps it hidden from students while you prepare it
visibility  'enrolled' (default) or 'public'

resources.title: Week 1 Live Class - Get Techy With Lucky
resources.description: Tuesday 8 September, 7:30-9:30pm UTC on Google Meet. Bring the Week 1 student guide.
resources.objective: Join the live session and work through the Week 1 material with the group.

resources.title: Web Fundamentals Training Manual
resources.description: The 71-page foundation manual: how the internet works, frontend vs backend, website anatomy, design principles, and a preview of every technology in the course.
resources.objective: Explain how the web works end to end, and place every later week in the context of the whole stack.

resources.title: How the Internet & the Web Work - Student Guide
resources.description: Your written companion to the live session: the physical internet and packets, IP addresses and DNS, HTTP and HTTPS requests, and how a browser turns code into a rendered page.
resources.objective: Follow the live session with notes in hand, and trace a page load from the address bar to the screen.

resources.title: HTML & Semantic HTML Master Guide
resources.description: Complete HTML reference: foundations, core elements, attributes, semantic structure, accessibility and a full quiz.
resources.objective: Structure any page with correct, meaningful HTML rather than a pile of divs.

resources.title: How the Internet & the Web Actually Work - Masterclass Notes
resources.description: Instructor delivery notes for the Week 1 masterclass: the four-module arc, the no-code hooks, the technical deconstruction and the timed activities.
resources.objective: Deliver the Week 1 masterclass with the hooks, activities and timings prepared.

resources.title: Welcome to Web Development
resources.description: The opening session deck: what web development is, what a developer actually does day to day, how the course is structured and what you will have built by Week 8.
resources.objective: Describe what web development involves and how the eight weeks fit together.

resources.title: How the Internet and the Web Actually Work
resources.description: The live session deck walking through clients and servers, DNS, HTTP requests and responses, and what happens between typing a URL and seeing a page.
resources.objective: Trace a page load end to end, from the address bar to the rendered result.

resources.title: HTML Quick Reference Notes
resources.description: A condensed revision sheet covering the HTML essentials in a few pages. Use it for revision, not as a replacement for the master guide.
resources.objective: Recall HTML syntax quickly while building, without re-reading the full guide.

resources.title: CSS Foundations & Responsive Design
resources.description: Selectors, the cascade, specificity, the box model, Flexbox, CSS Grid and mobile-first responsive design, with 48 key terms, a quiz and the weekly assignment.
resources.objective: Turn semantic HTML into a professional, responsive interface using hand-written CSS.

resources.title: Tailwind CSS & Modern Frontend Development
resources.description: Why frameworks exist, utility-first styling, configuring a brand design system, component thinking, plus terminology, a quiz and the weekly assignment.
resources.objective: Build and configure a Tailwind project, and know when to extract a repeated pattern into a component.

resources.title: JavaScript Complete Master Guide
resources.description: Sixteen chapters from variables through the DOM, events, forms, ES6+, async JavaScript, error handling and modules, ending in a comprehensive quiz.
resources.objective: Make a page interactive: manipulate the DOM, respond to events, and work with data.

resources.title: Git & GitHub Workflow
resources.description: Version control from first principles: the snapshot model, the three areas, branching, merge conflicts, pull requests, and the files every repository needs.
resources.objective: Work confidently with branches and pull requests, and recover safely when something goes wrong.

resources.title: Single-Page Application Build Guide
resources.description: A guided build: the HTML skeleton, the CSS switch logic, a vanilla JavaScript router and a hamburger menu, with a quiz, project brief and marking rubric.
resources.objective: Build a working single-page application with a JavaScript router, without a framework.

resources.title: Forms, Authentication & HTTP Methods
resources.description: HTML forms, login and registration pages, authentication versus authorization, HTTP methods, JavaScript validation and security fundamentals. Sets up the backend auth work in Weeks 5 and 6.
resources.objective: Build and validate a form, and explain what happens between the browser and the server when a user logs in.

resources.title: PHP Complete Master Guide
resources.description: Sixteen chapters covering PHP syntax, control flow, functions, arrays, strings, form handling, superglobals, file handling, object-oriented PHP, sessions and authentication, security and MVC structure.
resources.objective: Write server-side PHP that handles form data, manages sessions and authenticates users safely.

resources.title: MySQL & Database Management Master Guide
resources.description: Eighteen chapters from relational theory through DDL, DML, joins, subqueries, constraints, indexes, transactions, normalization, security and PHP integration with PDO.
resources.objective: Design a normalised database and query it safely from PHP using prepared statements.

resources.title: Deployment, Docker & DevOps
resources.description: SDLC and Agile, environments and environment variables, DNS and SSL, deploying static and PHP applications, containers and Docker Compose, CI/CD, monitoring and production security.
resources.objective: Take a project from your laptop to a live, secured, documented deployment.

resources.title: Capstone Project Guide & Brief
resources.description: The full capstone specification: choosing a scope you can finish, the seven stages, database design, the security checklist, the marking rubric and the presentation guide.
resources.objective: Plan, build, test, deploy, document and defend a complete full-stack application.
